description: Found in defk-9p6.16 (examples/gorilla_encode.exs). Measured under load, best of 15 over 10k calls on a 1-point input: a kernel returning len(p) as an i64 costs 0.015-0.04 us per call; the same kernel returning <<len(p)::8>> as a bitstring costs 0.12-0.17 us; Gorilla.Kernels.streams on 1 and 2 points 0.15-0.17 us, on 100 points 0.68 us. At gorilla_stream's realistic size (100-point blocks) one defk encode is ~2.1 us, so this fixed cost is ~5% of defk's time on a verdict that sits at 1.96-2.38x. Suspects, not profiled: defk_bits_reserve starting a 64-byte owned binary and doubling with enif_realloc_binary + memset (64 -> 128 -> 256 -> 512 for a ~450-byte output), the copy of the bits into the result binary, and the generated wrapper's <<b::bitstring-size(len), _::bitstring>> match. Minimal repro: defk bits1(p :: [i64]) :: bitstring do acc = <<>>; <<acc::bitstring, len(p)::8>> end against defk one(p :: [i64]) :: i64 do len(p) end, timed over 10k calls each.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Find and cut the ~0.1 us fixed per-call cost of a kernel that returns a bitstring

**Current behavior:**
Under load, best of 15 over 10k calls: `defk one(p :: [i64]) :: i64 do len(p) end` costs 0.015-0.04 us per call; `defk bits1(p :: [i64]) :: bitstring do acc = <<>>; <<acc::bitstring, len(p)::8>> end` costs 0.12-0.17 us. At gorilla_encode's realistic size this is ~5% of defk's time. Suspects (not profiled): the accumulator starting as a 64-byte owned binary and doubling with realloc + memset, the copy of the bits into the result binary, and the generated wrapper's match of the result.

**Desired behavior:**
- Profile first: attribute the extra time among the suspects (and anything else found), e.g. by variants of the repro and the generated C/wrapper, timed with interleaved repeats.
- Fix the parts that are worth it without changing results or the runtime contract (e.g. a better initial size, avoiding a copy, a cheaper result path). If no fix is worth it, the measurements are the result.
- Record findings, including what did not help, in docs/performance.md (provisional if loaded).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A breakdown of the per-call cost of bits1 vs one, with numbers
- [ ] If changed: bits1's per-call cost before/after, gorilla_encode before/after, and all bitstring tests and agreement tests pass, also under forced yields
- [ ] `mix test`, `mix docs`, `mix credo --strict` clean

**Out of scope:**
- New bitstring segment kinds (defk-pe3); the general NIF call overhead of scalar kernels

Profiled with bench/bits_call_cost.exs (per call, best of 15 over 100k calls, load 4-5): scalar 15 ns, empty bitstring 27 ns, one-byte bitstring 125 ns, alloc(u8,1) returned 105 ns. The cost is the owned-buffer machinery, not the bitstring: ~50 ns is the enif_realloc + enif_free of the ctx->owned table. Fix: the first 4 slots live in the frame (DEFK_OWNED_INLINE), the heap table starts at the fifth buffer, defk_promote re-points the table when the frame moves. After: one-byte bitstring 60-70 ns, alloc(u8,1) 58-62 ns; gorilla_encode 2.206 -> 2.06 ms (provisional). Not adopted: a 256-byte initial accumulator (mixed, within noise). Test added in test/owned_budget_test.exs (table growth with and without a yield). Full suite green; mix ci running.

title: A kernel that returns a bitstring costs ~0.1 us more per call than a scalar kernel
